newsitem.title: SWEDEN: France's REGIONAL airlines orders 2 Saab aircraft.
newsitem.headline: France's REGIONAL airlines orders 2 Saab aircraft.

text.p: Sweden's Saab Aircraft said on Monday that France's REGIONAL airlines had ordered a further two Saab 2000 JetProps to add to its fleet of four plus a fifth to be delivered in October.
Nantes-based Regional operates eight Saab 340s and other smaller aircraft, making it France's largest independent regional airline, Saab Aircraft AB said in a statement.

"The two new aircraft -- one scheduled for April 1997 delivery and the second for August -- have been ordered to cope with the operator's rapidly growing national and international route network, as well as to take over some existing 30 seat routes where passenger loads have increased," it said.
Saab Aircraft information director Anders Annerfalk told Reuters the deal was worth around $30 million.
"The list price of a Saab 2000 is $15 million. Regional Airlines' order is entirely new. It does not exploit any existing options and there are no new options in the order," Annerfalk said.
Saab Aircraft is part of the Saab Group, wholly owned by Swedish investment company Investor.
